label: Text 1
transcript: Maja read a 1,200-word piece by an English-language outlet on a contested local protest. She underlined the verbs of attribution. By the end she had counted: said 11 times, insisted 3, claimed 4, denied 1, added 2. She wrote in the margin: verbs of attribution are votes.

label: Text 2
transcript: Long-form journalism is, mostly, a question of framing and verbs. The frame is what the article treats as the question; everything before the subhead is doing frame work. The verbs of attribution carry, accordingly, more weight than their dictionary definitions suggest. Said is neutral; claimed signals doubt; insisted signals stubbornness; added signals subordination. A reader who counts the verbs already knows half the writer's argument before they reach the conclusion.
